BiblicalUsage: Pharaoh's chariots sank like lead in the mighty waters, and Moses sings of it. Jeremiah sank in the mire of the dungeon pit, and the psalmist cries, I sink in deep mire, where there is no standing. David's stone sank into Goliath's forehead. The word is sinking, going down: into water, into mud, into the earth, into death.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that sinking is the Bible's picture of being beyond one's own rescue. I believe the psalmist's cry is the right prayer for it: I sink, and only God's hand reaches that deep. The same God who sank Pharaoh's army lifted Jeremiah out of the pit.
